cf.title: Fix out-of-bounds access in pg_bsd_indent's parser stack

input.subject: [PATCH v1] Fix out-of-bounds access in pg_bsd_indent's parser stack

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The problem is stated in message #1, and message #3 reproduces a segfault that filled a disk and confirms the patch turns it into a "Parser stack overflow" error. The fix changes two array sizes and one bound check in a developer tool, so it adds no cost for server users. Confidence is medium because no one has reviewed the code yet.

brief.title: Fix out-of-bounds writes in pg_bsd_indent parser stack arrays
brief.problem: pg_bsd_indent indexes three arrays in parser_state (p_stack, il, cstk) with one shared index, tos, but checks overflow only against p_stack, the largest. Deeply nested input can therefore write past the end of il and cstk. This affects developers who run pgindent on source code.
brief.proposed_design: The patch sizes il and cstk at 256 entries, the same as p_stack. It also makes the overflow check one element stricter, because the lbrace case pushes two entries (lbrace, then stmt) in one call to parse().
user_visible_surface: pg_bsd_indent now stops with "Parser stack overflow" on deeply nested input instead of crashing.
author_claims: The overflow check used only p_stack, so cstk and il could be accessed out of bounds.
Giving all three arrays the same size closes the gap.
The lbrace case needs room for two more entries when parse() starts.
brief.thread_state: Daniel Gustafsson asked for a reproducer. Álvaro Herrera built one with 256 nested if statements and a switch, which segfaulted and filled his disk; with the patch, pg_bsd_indent stops with "Parser stack overflow". No one has reviewed the code yet.
unclear: The CommitFest entry targets version 16, but the thread does not say which branches should get the fix.
The thread does not say whether other pushes in parse() can add more than two entries per call.
The thread does not say whether the reproducer should become a regression test for pg_bsd_indent.
The thread does not say whether anyone checked this against upstream FreeBSD indent.

questions: Which branches should get the fix, given that the CommitFest entry targets version 16?
Can any other path in parse() push more than two entries per call, so that the "- 2" bound is still too loose?
Should the reproducer from message #3 become a regression test for pg_bsd_indent?

committability.owner_note: Daniel Gustafsson and Álvaro Herrera take part in the thread, and Álvaro tested the patch in message #3; neither has reviewed the code. The owner needs to know the pg_bsd_indent parser and pgindent.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a bounds fix in a developer tool: that the new check covers every push in parse(), and that pgindent output does not change. A back-patch extends this to each branch that carries the tool.
committability.author_follow_up: No sign either way; the author does not post again in the visible messages after message #1.

priority.reason: The patch changes three lines in two files of a developer tool and has a confirmed reproducer in message #3. It helps only developers who run pgindent, but it adds no user-visible surface and little to maintain.

provisional_note: Only the diff in message #1 was read, not the rest of parse.c. Whether every push in parse() and every use of il and cstk stays within the new bounds could not be checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add code indentation check to cirrus-ci
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a Cirrus CI task, or a step in the SanityCheck or CompilerWarnings task, that runs pgindent and fails when a change is not pgindent-clean. The goal is to catch indentation problems in developer and cfbot CI runs before commit, so that committers spend less time on follow-up indentation fixes.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the CI check puts the burden of pgindent-cleanliness on initial patch submitters, while it should be enforced at commit into the master repo. He feared it would drive novice contributors away. Andrew Dunstan saw no consensus for the change, and the author withdrew the CF entry because the idea was being discussed in a separate thread about meson targets for pgindent.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
We want to enforce this at commit into the master repo, but
I fear enforcing it earlier will drive novice contributors away for
no very good reason.

precedents_retrieved.title: Show subtransaction overflow status
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch exposes each backend's subtransaction count and whether its subtransaction cache has overflowed, so DBAs can find the sessions that force SLRU lookups for all concurrent queries. It started as two new pg_stat_activity columns and was reworked into a single function returning a record per backend.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane argued that effort should go into fixing the subtransaction overflow performance problem itself, because monitoring does not relieve the problem and could cause compatibility problems once a fundamental fix changes how this area works. Andres Freund agreed and asked for the entry to be marked rejected, also noting it had been failing on cfbot for weeks. The author agreed that a real fix would make the status reporting pointless and marked it rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If the subxact overflow business is causing
real-world performance problems, let's find a way to fix that, not put
effort into monitoring tools that do little to actually alleviate anyone's
pain.

precedents_retrieved.title: Nonreplayable XLog records by means of overflows and >MaxAllocSize lengths
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds checks in xloginsert.c so that the WAL insertion API cannot assemble a record larger than xlogreader can read (MaxAllocSize, later a fixed 1020 MiB limit), and cannot overflow xl_tot_len through repeated XLogRegisterData() calls. It also documents the record size limit in the XLogRecord spec.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier committed part of the patch, the API changes and the uint16 block data checks. He then asked for a rebase of the rest, and the author did not reply for two commitfests, so the entry was returned with feedback. After it was closed, Andres Freund noted that the new record-too-large ERROR usually happens inside a critical section and so becomes a PANIC. He suggested building large records such as the commit record before the critical section.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
No replies after 4 weeks, so I have marked this entry as returned
with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve overflow checks potentially optimized away by compiler
precedents_retrieved.summary: The proposal rewrites signed-integer overflow checks such as x + y < x into precondition tests such as x > INT_MAX - y, so compilers that treat signed overflow as undefined (icc, pathcc, clang) cannot remove them. Later versions extended this to int.c, int8.c and btree_gist, added INT16 overflow macros and added regression tests.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No reviewer took up the final version, so Michael Paquier marked it returned with feedback. Earlier, Greg Stark wrote that he was coming around to Tom's view that the change was a lot of hassle for little gain. Tom's own message giving that view is not among the visible messages.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: And nobody got interested into that, marking as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: prefetching for nestloop / indexscan
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an ExecPrefetch executor callback so that a nested loop reads a batch of outer rows and asks a parameterized inner index scan to prefetch the matching heap pages. It is a small proof of concept limited to nestloop with an inner index scan, controlled by a new enable_nestloop_prefetch setting.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry because the patch was a quick experiment and he had no time to keep working on it. Before that, Andres Freund questioned the extra executor tree traversals and suggested passing multiple values down in one parameter, possibly as one ScalarArrayOps index scan. Peter Geoghegan supported that direction. The author agreed it looks like block nested loop join, which moves the work away from this design, and his cached-data benchmark showed about a 30% regression.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
But
the patch was just a quick & dirty experiment, I don't have time to work
on this right now.

precedents_retrieved.title: Optimize Numeric using fixed buffer reducing pallocs for small numbers
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a small fixed digit buffer to NumericVar, with a buf_len field, so that small numerics avoid palloc/pfree in numeric.c. Later versions reuse allocated buffers and change add_var(), div_var() and similar functions so the result may no longer be one of the operands.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Dean Rasheed found the change too invasive for gains of a few percent, with regressions in some cases such as generate_series() and a sqrt/sum series. He objected to low-level functions no longer accepting the result as an input, and proposed instead to reuse the digit buffer in make_result(); Joel Jacobson agreed to abandon the fixed buffer approach. No one pursued the alternative patch, and Peter Eisentraut returned the entry as inactive.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So IMO the results just don't justify such an extensive set of
changes, and I think we should abandon this fixed buffer approach.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix buffer pinning logic/visibility bugs in [SP-]Gist Index-Only Scans
precedents_retrieved.authors: Peter Geoghegan (pgeoghegan), Michail Nikolaev (nkey), Matthias van de Meent (mmeent), Mihail Nikalayeu (mihailnikalayeu)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes a race in GiST and SP-GiST index-only scans, where concurrent VACUUM can remove a TID and set the visibility map bit before the scan checks it, so a dead tuple is returned. Later versions drop the idea of holding pins on index pages: they add a table AM API (table_index_vischeck_tuples) so the index AM checks the visibility map while it still holds the page pin, and they also change nbtree to use it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last visible message (v14, December 2025) only fixes a CFBot failure, and the entry was withdrawn about six months later with no visible objection or explanation. The author had moved a backpatchable version of the fix to a separate thread.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix out-of-bounds with function PQescapeInternal
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the buffer size that PQescapeInternal in libpq allocates on its slow path, adding two bytes per quote or backslash. It followed a Coverity report of an out-of-bounds write in pg_createsubscriber.c.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane replied that each quote or backslash is already counted in input_len, so one extra byte per character is enough. He added an Assert that the buffer is filled exactly, and check-world passed. The author checked with a debugger, found no overrun, called the Coverity warning wrong, and withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Nonsense.  The quote or backslash is already counted in input_len,
so we need to add just one more.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert support for improved tracking of nested queries
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert support for improved tracking of nested queries
Reverted commit(s): Track more precisely query locations for nested statements; Fix regression with location calculation of nested statements; pg_stat_statements: Add tests for nested queries with level tracking
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This commit reverts the two following commits:
- 499edb09741b, track more precisely query locations for nested
statements.
- 06450c7b8c70, a follow-up fix of 499edb09741b with query locations.
The test introduced in this commit is not reverted.  This is proving
useful to track a problem that only pgaudit was able to detect.

These prove to have issues with the tracking of SELECT statements, when
these use multiple parenthesis which is something supported by the
grammar.  Incorrect location and lengths are causing pg_stat_statements
to become confused, failing its job in query normalization with
potential out-of-bound writes because the location and the length may
not match with what can be handled.  A lot of the query patterns
discussed when this issue was reported have no test coverage in the main
regression test suite, or the recovery test 027_stream_regress.pl would
have caught the problems as pg_stat_statements is loaded by the node
running the regression tests.  A first step would be to improve the test
coverage to stress more the query normalization logic.

A different portion of this work was done in 45e0ba30fc40, with the
addition of tests for nested queries.  These can be left in the tree.
They are useful to track the way inner queries are currently tracked by
PGSS with non-top-level entries, and will be useful when reconsidering
in the future the work reverted here.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent search returned no earlier attempt at this fix, and no thread message points to an earlier discussion. Nothing from the prior-attempts angle stands against this small bug fix, which message #3 confirms with a reproducer.

The patch fixes a crash in a developer-only tool. For input within the old limits it adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object, dump format or client-visible behaviour, and it does not change pgindent output. The stricter check only rejects nesting one level shallower than before, about 254 levels, which no real source file in the tree reaches. Branch targeting is a backpatch policy question, not a compatibility objection.

The patch changes only the in-memory parser_state struct of pg_bsd_indent, a developer tool that is not linked into the server or libpq. No on-disk format, WAL, catalog, wire protocol or extension ABI is touched, so nothing here crosses a process or machine boundary.

No objection from the security angle. pg_bsd_indent is a developer tool that runs locally on source files the developer chooses, so it has no privilege model, server exposure or user data. The patch makes deeply nested input stop with "Parser stack overflow" instead of writing out of bounds, which reduces risk, including the disk-filling crash shown in message #3.

This is a three-line bounds fix in a developer tool that is already in the tree, with a working reproducer in message #3. It adds no runtime cost to the server, no new API, and no external dependency. The larger arrays cost about 1 KiB in one struct, and any divergence from upstream indent is small and fixes a crash. Without the code I could not check whether other pushes in parse() add more than two entries per call, or which branches carry this tool.

This is a memory-safety bugfix in pg_bsd_indent, a tool that ships in the source tree. No other feature, option or extension already gives this fix, so no existing alternative applies. Whether to use upstream FreeBSD indent instead is a separate question that the material does not raise.

This is a memory-safety bugfix in a project tool, and the demand angle does not apply in the usual way. Message #3 reproduces a segfault that filled a disk, and the fix changes only the sizes of two arrays and one bound check, so it adds no user surface or maintenance cost to weigh against the size of the user group.
